# Results — Study 905 (Residual Reversal)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — Blitz,
Huij, Lansdorp & Verbeek (2013): the raw one-week reversal is contaminated by bid-ask
bounce and common-factor moves, so reverse on the **market-model residual** instead, on a
liquid subset. Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to
reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month; the
partial current month is dropped; as-of 2026-06-30). Fingerprint `357fd262912f` (panel Close).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily OHLC **+ Volume** (`auto_adjust=True`, total-return), **50 liquid US large-caps**, 2010-01-04 → 2026-06-30, **4,147** dated rows/name → **861** weekly (W-FRI) returns |
| Universe | a fixed `UNIVERSE` of ~50 mega-caps, pulled through the **`quantlab.universe` survivorship guard** (`download_panel(..., allow_survivorship_bias=True)`), cached under this study's own `_cache/` |
| Signal | each name's **weekly market-model residual** — weekly return minus a trailing-52-week rolling-OLS fit on the equal-weight market (`r − α − β·mkt`), known at the close of `w−1` (one `shift`) |
| Sort | each week keep the **top 60% by trailing dollar volume**, then **long the bottom 30%** (residual losers), **short the top 30%** (residual winners), equal-weight; earn week-`w` raw return |
| Foil | the **raw** weekly reversal (sort on last week's raw return, same screen) placed beside the residual version |
| Execution / costs | one documented lag: signal through close `w−1` → hold week `w`. The costed timer charges 2 sides × one-way × NAV per **weekly** rebalance (near-full turnover); the short book pays 50 bps/yr borrow |
| Statistics | Newey-West (HAC, 8-lag) *t* on the weekly spread; one-sample *t*; Welch *t* on the pooled loser-vs-winner books; a 1,000-permutation placebo; a 20-seed synthetic positive control |

**Survivorship — named on the Signal axis.** `UNIVERSE` is a **current-membership** list
of names that are liquid mega-caps *today*, so the magnitudes are an **upper bound**.
Crucially, short-term reversal is documented as a **small-cap / illiquid-breadth**
phenomenon; a 50-mega-cap survivor panel is exactly where it is *least* likely to appear —
which is what we find.

## The headline — long residual-loser / short residual-winner spread

Weekly equal-weight bottom-30% minus top-30% market-model-residual spread on the top-60%
dollar-volume subset (n = **808** weeks, median 30 names/week):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| **spread (long residual-loser − short residual-winner)** | **−0.38 bps/week** |
| Newey-West(8) *t* | **−0.05** |
| one-sample *t* | −0.04 |
| loser book / winner book | +34.12 bps / +34.51 bps (Welch *t* = −0.03) |
| gross spread Sharpe (no cost) | −0.01 · hit-rate 51.1% |

**The cleaned signal is a flat line.** The residual reversal — factor-stripped and
liquidity-screened exactly as Blitz et al prescribe — is statistically indistinguishable
from zero. And the cleaning does not rescue anything, because there was nothing to rescue:

| variant | spread | NW *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| **residual reversal** (liquid, factor-cleaned) | −0.38 bps/wk | **−0.05** |
| **raw** weekly reversal (same screen) | −0.03 bps/wk | −0.00 |
| residual reversal, **no** liquidity screen | +2.31 bps/wk | +0.32 |

Raw and residual are both dead; dropping the screen nudges the residual to +2.31 bps/week
but still at *t* = +0.32 — noise. On 50 liquid mega-caps there is simply no weekly
reversal, clean or dirty, to harvest.

## Placebo — is the (non-)result a lucky alignment of the sort?

Keep the residual-reversal sort but read each week's forward returns from a
**column-permuted** panel (signal → outcome link broken), 1,000 permutations (20 seeds ×
50):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| observed spread | **−0.38 bps** |
| placebo mean (sd) | +0.063 bps (5.348) |
| right-tail *p* | **0.513** (dead centre) |

The observed spread sits in the dead centre of the permutation null — no evidence of any
signal, in either direction.

## Robustness — two eras (split 2018-01-01)

| era | spread | NW *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| 2010-01 → 2018-01 (n=364) | +2.18 bps | +0.26 |
| 2018-01 → 2026-06 (n=443) | −3.18 bps | −0.23 |

The spread **flips sign** across the two halves and is insignificant in both — the
hallmark of no effect, not a fragile one.

## The timer — can you get paid for it?

Charge 2 sides × one-way × NAV per weekly rebalance (a weekly reversal turns over almost
fully); short pays 50 bps/yr borrow.

| one-way cost | gross/wk | cost/wk | net/wk | *t* (net) | Sharpe (net) | ~ann. |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **1 bp** | −0.38 bps | 2.96 bps | **−3.35 bps** | −0.39 | −0.10 | −1.7%/yr |
| **5 bps** | −0.38 bps | 10.96 bps | **−11.35 bps** | −1.32 | −0.33 | −5.9%/yr |

A gross edge of ~zero cannot survive a fully-turning weekly book's friction; even the
un-screened +2.31 bps/week gross is eaten several times over by the 2.96 bps/week
round-trip at a mere 1 bp. **Mirage.**

## Synthetic positive control — the cleaner works, the null is real

Deterministic seeded panel: each name loads on a strong common factor (`β_i`) and carries
a weekly residual with a planted mean-reversion (AR(1) coefficient `−edge`). No network.

| world | residual NW *t* | raw NW *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| null (`edge = 0`), **20 seeds** | mean **+0.17** (sd 0.78), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 0/20** | — |
| planted (`edge = 0.35`, seed 905) | **+24.99** | +13.23 (factor-muddied) |

The residual detector recovers a *planted* reversal cleanly and **above** the raw detector
(the factor genuinely muddies the raw sort — the mechanism Blitz et al describe), and never
fires on the null. So the flat real-tape result is a genuine **absence of edge on
mega-caps**, not a broken engine. *(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in
support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** On 50 liquid US mega-caps the factor-cleaned, liquidity-screened
  weekly residual reversal earns **−0.38 bps/week** (NW *t* = **−0.05**) — a flat line. The
  raw foil is equally dead (−0.03 bps), the placebo is dead-centre (*p* = 0.51), and the
  two eras flip sign (*t* = +0.26 / −0.23). The 20-seed synthetic control recovers a
  *planted* residual reversal cleanly (*t* = +24.99, above the factor-muddied raw *t* =
  +13.23; fires on 0/20 nulls), so the null is real: short-term reversal is a
  small/illiquid-breadth effect, absent in mega-caps. Survivorship biases the magnitude
  upward — and it is still zero.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** A ~zero gross edge cannot survive the 2.96 bps/week round-trip
  friction of a fully-turning weekly book: net −3.35 bps/wk at 1 bp, −11.35 at 5 bps.
